utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we can start? I can't see everyone's tile.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'm here. Was on mute.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Good. So, uh, first thing, the printer on two. Abena says the contractor comes Thursday-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thursday or Friday? I had Friday.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Maybe Thursday. I'll check the email.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Because I'm out Friday morning for the badge thing anyway.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is that the one that jammed all last month?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so. There's two on that floor though.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: One on two, and the old one by the stairs. The old one's dead.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right. Big picture we probably just need fewer of them.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Or ones that work.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Ha, yes. Okay, um, anyway, moving on. The flooring.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Finally.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: So the ground floor, reception and the corridors, I think maybe we need to - we've got until-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: End of November. Before the January client visits.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right, thank you. So where did we land, Dmitri, you had the sheet?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Only the timber quote. Davor sent it over.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: The engineered timber?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yeah. Sixty-one a metre, fitted. That's what we pencilled in.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Mm. It felt steep when we first saw it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: It's, well, it's a lot of floor, so.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Sorry, can I - what about vinyl plank? The luxury sort, all 420 metres, glued down.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Vinyl. In reception.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not the bathroom-lino stuff, the proper-

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I know what it is. I'm just saying clients walk in and see vinyl.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Hang on, let me finish. Chidi priced it around thirty-eight a metre fitted, against the sixty-one for the timber, and they'd be in and out in three days. Fifteen years of warranty on top.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Three days, that's quick.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Warranty on what, though? Wear layer, or the glue, or-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'd have to look. The paperwork says fifteen.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Timber was two weeks, I think. Davor said.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, so, much less disruption.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, glued down means if one plank goes, you're ripping up a section.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: They keep spare boxes. That's standard-

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Standard until the batch changes.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I think maybe that's fair, Sofia, but, um, the same is true of the timber, no?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Less so. You can sand timber.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Honestly, for the corridors it feels like it doesn't matter. Trolleys, deliveries, it takes a beating.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Trolleys are the big thing. Umar's team brings the post cart through every morning.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Which is why vinyl, it doesn't dent.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Timber dents. Okay, I'll give you that.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay. Um. Does anyone know if... the sub-floor's even? Because glue-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Jamal said it's screed, fairly flat. He walked it in September.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh good. That's, yes. I forgot he did that.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: See, so-

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Hold on, I just want to - sorry, Amara - what's the lead time on the planks?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Two weeks, give or take. Chidi said he could order Monday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That works with November?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Easily.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: What about the look? Reception's the first thing people see.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Honestly the good ones look like wood. You can't tell from standing.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: From standing. Fine. Not from kneeling.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Nobody's kneeling in reception.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Ha.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, so, um, money. What does that even come to, thirty-eight times, uh-

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sixteen thousand, give or take?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Sixteen-ish. And the timber was, what, like twenty-five?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Closer to twenty-six.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right. Right.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So you're saving ten thousand to put down something I'd call a bit cheap-looking.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's not cheap-looking, it's - Sofia, have you seen the sample?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's in my bag, I'll show you after.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fine. I'll look at the sample.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I ask something totally unrelated? Who's doing the kitchen order this week?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, um, I think maybe Jamal?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Jamal's off. I'll do it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We're out of the oat milk, apparently people have opinions.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'll add it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And the good teabags, not the-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'll add the good ones.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Thank you, Dmitri. Okay, and, uh, the visitor passes. Reception ran out again.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: How do you run out of visitor passes?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: People take them home, I think.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: They put them in coat pockets. It's a known thing.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Someone should do an amnesty.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Ha, maybe. I'll ask Abena to order more.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is Abena back from leave?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Monday, I think. Or Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Monday. She told me.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Monday, good.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay can we go back to the floor? Because I'm not going to pretend I'm over it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, sure, yes. Um.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, we've been circling this since September. Whatever gets it done before the visits.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm not against doing it. I just don't want it looking like a car park.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It won't look like a car park.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: The sample I saw in Chidi's showroom looked okay. Sort of a grey oak.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: You went to the showroom?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: In the summer. For the other building.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Huh. Fine. That's a point in favour.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: So, um, where does that leave... I think maybe we're mostly, kind of there?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I think we are.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fine by me if the sample's decent.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Fine with me.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay. So the luxury vinyl plank for the ground floor, reception and corridors, that's the floor. I'll let Chidi know.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Great. I'll send him the floor plan tonight.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Perfect. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Who's got the all-hands slides Thursday?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, me, I think. Maybe Umar.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Umar did the last ones.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Then maybe not Umar. I'll ask.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Whatever you do, keep the building bit short. Nobody cares about the printer.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Ha. True.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I need to jump, I've got a call with the alarm company.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, yes, go. Thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye all.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Don't forget the sample, Amara.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: In the bag, I said.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, um, can everyone hear me? Dmitri, you're on mute, I think.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Sorry. Better now.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Good. So, uh, first the all-hands thing, because Umar wants an answer today.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: The slides again?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: No, the follow-up. A building update, maybe two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Two minutes is generous for the building.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Just say the printer's fixed.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Is the printer fixed?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Contractor came Friday. Printed a test page, then jammed on the second one.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: So no.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture it's mostly fixed.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Mostly fixed isn't a thing with printers.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I'll say it's in progress. That's, yeah, safe.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fine. Can we do the floor? Elif, you had something from the survey.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, yes, um, sorry, that was next on my list anyway.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right, so Alejandra's people finished the slab survey yesterday. I only got the summary this morning.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Slab survey? We had one of those?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: They drilled and tested, readings all across the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Jamal said the screed was fine though.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Flat, yes. Flat's not the same as dry.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, so what came back?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: West half is fine. The east half read five point eight percent moisture, and the glue maker's ceiling is four and a half, so on that side the vinyl warranty is void unless we put a damp-proof layer down first, which is roughly fourteen a metre extra.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fourteen on top of thirty-eight.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yeah, give or take, for the east half only.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: How much of the floor is east?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: About half. The reception side, mostly.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh. Um. That's, I mean, that's the front, so.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Hang on, though. Chidi does this all the time. He lays a membrane, the glue's fine, we're covered.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: If we add the membrane, yes. That's the fourteen.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: So it's fifty-two with it. Sorry, I'm doing it in my head. Fifty-ish.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Fifty-two, I get.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Right, whatever, close to that.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Which is interesting.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Don't.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm only saying. Vinyl plus membrane, it's the same money as the other thing we looked at in the summer.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: The, um, the concrete?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Polished concrete. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Wait, we looked at that?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Davor mentioned it when he sent the timber quote. As an aside.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I think maybe I have the number somewhere. Let me look.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I don't see why we reopen this because of some damp. Membrane, done.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Because glued vinyl on a slab that wet doesn't hold. The edges start lifting inside two years, and when it does, nobody's paying, because the warranty's gone the moment the readings are over the limit.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: With a membrane it's covered.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: A membrane on a slab nobody's dried. I've seen it, Amara. Corners curl, it ripples by the door.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Reception's where the door is.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, right. That's, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay but you can't know it'd lift.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I can't know. Neither can you. That's sort of the point.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I jump in with something totally separate? Sorry. Is anyone going to the supplier thing on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Which supplier thing?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Cleaning. The tender walk-round.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, I think maybe Abena's covering that.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: She's back, so yes.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Great. I'll leave it with her.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Are we done? Because I'd like to finish this floor.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Sofia, you said concrete. Is that actually a serious idea or a, you know, a thought?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's serious. Look, polished and sealed, nothing gets glued, so the damp doesn't touch it. It's about fifty-two a metre, so the same as fixing the vinyl, and it'll last twenty-five years where vinyl's good for fifteen on a good day.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Twenty-five. Hm.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: The vinyl warranty says fifteen.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Warranty. Not life. Fifteen if the slab behaves.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Concrete takes trolleys fine. Better than anything.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's cold though. Reception, in January.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's a floor, not a sofa.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, and the noise, I think? Hard surface, the post cart.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Cart's rubber wheels. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And if it cracks?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Hairline, maybe. It's sealed. They grind it, they don't pour it. It's the slab we already have.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's a plus, no tearing up.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: How long does it take? Vinyl was three days.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Longer. A week and a half, maybe two. Grinding, then the sealing coats.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Before the visits?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: End of November, if they start soon. I'd want it in writing.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Hm. Right. Who even does it? Chidi doesn't, do they?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: He doesn't. He subcontracts it. I can ask.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Davor would know someone.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I can message Davor now.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is there a look thing? Sofia was worried about vinyl in reception.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I was. Concrete's the grown-up version, honestly. Warm grey, a bit of sheen.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fine. I'll give you that it looks decent.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: But I sent Chidi the floor plan last week. He's expecting this.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: He's not ordered anything though, has he?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not that I know. He said Monday, then I think it slipped.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right. Good. Um.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: If we're pricing, concrete's what, twenty-two thousand?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Over twenty, anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: And the vinyl plus membrane would be, um, I don't know, twenty-ish as well.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not so different, no.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And one of them might peel off the floor.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Let me think about this properly. The damp's not going away, and nobody wants to be back here in two winters with a curling floor. So, yes, polished concrete for the ground floor. I'll tell Chidi it's off.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Fine. I'll call him, it's my mess anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, would you? Thank you, Amara.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'll hear back from Davor this afternoon, probably.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Good. Big picture, we've lost about a week on this.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: We found out about the damp before it was glued down. That's not a loss.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else? The kitchen order, is that sorted?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Done. Oat milk's coming.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Good teabags?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Good teabags.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Lovely. Okay, I need to run to a thing. Thanks all.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe we're all here? Elif, I can hear your kettle.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Muting.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: No, it's fine. So, uh, before the floor, the fire drill. Abena wants a date.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not the week of the client visits, obviously.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right, right, that's, yes. I think maybe the second week of December?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fine by me. Nobody's here in the second week of December anyway.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, as long as it's not a Monday.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Not a Monday. I'll tell her Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Wednesday's the day the post cart's late. Umar's team does the sorting then.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh. Then, um, Thursday?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Thursday's fine.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Can we get to the floor? I've got a call at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. So, um, Dmitri, you were out at the site on Monday, I think?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yeah. Went with Alejandra's lot. The contractor did a trial patch.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: A trial patch of what, the grinding?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Grinding and sealing, a couple of square metres each side. One by the stairwell, one in the east end.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: West was fine. Took the grind, came up nice. Grey, sort of even.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Good. So that's the answer then.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's the east that's, um. Hang on, I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: The screed over there is thin. Like six millimetres, they measured it. And when the grinder went across it, it just, it came away. Powdery.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Came away how much?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Enough that you'd be polishing the sand layer. So they won't seal that half as it is. They want a topping laid first, a new skim. About twenty-one a metre on top of the fifty-two.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: On the whole floor?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: No, the east half. West doesn't need it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh. Um. That's, right. That's the front again, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Reception side, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm still on the number. Twenty-one on half?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Half the floor, yeah. Contractor's emailing it properly this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: So did they say it's a big job? The topping?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Extra few days. Needs to cure before they grind.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Hm. I think maybe we should hear from Amara, she looked unhappy.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'm not unhappy, I'm doing the sum. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's about sixty-something a metre averaged. Round it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Don't help. I'm getting there.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I ask something else while she does that? Is anyone using the second meeting room tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, I don't think so. Why?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: The auditors want somewhere quiet for an hour.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Take it. I'll tell reception.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Does reception even have the booking sheet now?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Abena moved it. It's on the shared drive, I think.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Fine. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. So if it's fifty-two for the west and seventy-three for the east, that's, what, sixty-three across the lot. Call it sixty-three.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: That's about what I said.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And that's before anything else. Because it was never just the price.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Sorry, what do you mean, Amara?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: The hard surface. I went and looked at what Alejandra's team sent about the acoustics. With the polished concrete, reception comes out at one point nine seconds reverberation. The target is point eight. So it's more than double. You'd stand at the desk and every voice rings back. And now it's sixty-three a metre to get there.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: One point nine. Is that bad?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Point eight is what the brief says. It's, yeah, it's bad.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's an echo chamber, basically.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm not arguing. For once.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Rubber carpet tiles would fix the sound. In reception only.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: That's another cost, though.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I know. I'm just saying it's a thing.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe we, we shouldn't start adding things yet.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, is there a version where this is all fine?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: There's always a version.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I meant, like, is it ten percent worse or is it a disaster?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: The money's maybe thirteen, fourteen thousand more over the whole floor. The sound is just a failure on the target.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Um.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Did the acoustics people say what the target is for?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Phone calls at the desk. And the visitors waiting.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Right. That's the January visits again.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, nobody's going to measure the reverb on the day.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: They'll hear it, though.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Fair. I'd say it sounds like a gallery.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Galleries are fine. People like galleries.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not at the desk.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I think, um, maybe the topping is the thing I can't get my head round. Is that a proper material, or a patch?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Cement-based. Proper floor topping, they said. They'd lay it, then grind it, so the finish should match.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Should.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That's what he said. Should.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Hm.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, totally unrelated, but did anyone see the email about the security contract renewal?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I don't think I did. Is that us?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Might be Jamal's. I'll forward it.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's Jamal's. He's on it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Great, I'll leave it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Can we stay on this? I do have the call.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: The other thing is whether the timing still works. A topping adds cure time.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: He said about four or five days extra. So you'd have, hm, two weeks and a bit total, if they start on the third.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: The third of December?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: November. Monday the twenty-fourth, he said, if we confirm.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh. That's, um, that's not much room before the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Barely any.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'd want the dates in writing, like last time.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And Chidi's out. We told him it was off, he was fine about it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: He was, yes. Good.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Do we know what the other half of the building looks like? Upstairs?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Upstairs is carpet. Nobody's touching that.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Right. I just wondered if upstairs has the same screed.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Upstairs is a different pour. Jamal said.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Not helpful for us anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: No. I know.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay. So, um, where are we. I think maybe we can't really do anything today, can we? We've got new numbers, we've got the acoustics, and Dmitri's still waiting on the email.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'd want to see it written down before anyone says anything to anyone.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Agreed. I'm not saying throw it out. I'm saying look at it again.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Which is rich, coming from you, who wanted vinyl.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Vinyl had a damp problem. This has a thin screed problem and a noise problem. They're not the same.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Mm. I'll give you that.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Let's, um, look at this properly next week then. Dmitri, can you send round the contractor's email when it lands?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll forward it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: And Amara, the acoustics bit, if you can send that too.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Will do. I've got to drop, sorry. Call's starting.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Go, go. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think maybe that's everyone? Dmitri, I can see you, you're just, frozen.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'm here. Camera's being slow.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Good. So, uh, before anything, the parking, the visitor bays, Umar says-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Is this the bays by the side gate?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, the, the ones by the gate. He wants them marked before the visits.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Marked how? Big picture, do we even own those?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I think maybe half. Jamal would know.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Jamal's got the lease folder. He always has the lease folder.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: He's off till Monday.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right, then, um, it can wait. I'll ask when he's back.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Can I say something about the visits? The catering.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Is that, um, is that us?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Abena asked me to ask. Who's ordering sandwiches for the first one?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Not me. I do the sandwich thing every time.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: You do it very well, though.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's how it starts. Fine, send me the numbers.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'll find out how many are coming.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Lovely. Okay. Um. So the floor.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Here we go.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I know, I know. So, Chidi rang me yesterday, out of the blue, and he said, um, he said-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Chidi rang you? Why didn't he ring me?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I think maybe he had my number from the order thing. Anyway, he said there's a spray-on membrane now. Damp-proof. They spray it on the slab.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Instead of the sheet stuff?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, instead of the sheet. And the price he gave me was nine a metre.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Nine. Not fourteen.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Nine. I wrote it on my hand, basically.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Nine is a long way from fourteen. What's the catch?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: He said no catch. He can email it. Um, I forwarded nothing yet, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Nine a metre, on the east side only.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Well, that's the, that's the bit I wanted to ask. Because the west half read fine.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: West was under the limit, yes. Elif had the figures.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Four percent and a bit, I think. Under the glue ceiling anyway.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: So, right. I think maybe we have to look at this again, the whole floor, now that the number's different. Is everyone okay with that? Reopening it, I mean.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'm more than okay with it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Obviously you are.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Ha. Okay, so we are looking at it again, then. Fine. Good. Where do I even start?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Where we left it. Concrete with the topping, the sixty-three average.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Right, sixty-three. And, um, the reverb thing.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: The one point nine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Which I said was a gallery.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's not a gallery, it's a bathroom. Sorry. Go on, Sana.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: No, you, you were going to-

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, so the thing is, the east half is about two hundred and ten metres, yes? Half of four-twenty.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Two-ten, yes.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: So nine on two-ten is, hang on, eighteen ninety. About nineteen hundred pounds all in, on the whole job. That's it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: And Chidi says the manufacturer will put the warranty in writing if the spray goes down first, he's already asked them. So the fifteen years is back. And with the thirty-eight it's, what, forty-two a metre overall, near enough. Plus the acoustic-backed plank, which gets us under the point eight, so there's no echo problem at the desk.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on. Acoustic-backed. Who says it hits point eight?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: The data sheet. I can send it.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: A data sheet from the people selling it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's Alejandra's team's test method, I checked.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Hm. Fine. Say that's true.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Forty-two against sixty-three is a big gap.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Twenty-odd a metre, on four-twenty. That's eight thousand, nine?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, that's, yes, that's a lot.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, the slab is still wet. Nine pounds of spray doesn't dry it.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It doesn't need to dry it, it blocks it. That's the whole product.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Blocks it for how long?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Chidi said it's rated for the life of the floor. It's the same stuff they use in car parks.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Car parks. Great.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: In the good way, Sofia.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: What's it do to the timing? Spray needs to cure, I assume.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Day and a bit. He said he'd do it Monday, then the planks go on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: So, um, Monday the twenty-fourth?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Yes. Done by the end of that week, easily.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's actually better than the concrete.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Concrete was two weeks plus. This is under one.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Sofia, are you, um, is there still something that-

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: The edges. I'm still thinking about the edges at the door.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: With a membrane under the glue the edges are fine. That's the point of the warranty.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: In writing, you said.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: In writing. I'll forward the email the second I get it.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Is that the manufacturer's email or Chidi's?

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Chidi's covering note, and the manufacturer's letter attached. I think.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'd want to see the letter itself.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: You'll see it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, unrelated. Does anyone know if the lights in the corridor by the kitchen are on a timer?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: The corridor lights? Um, why?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: They were on at seven this morning and nobody was in.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Motion sensor's broken. I logged it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh good. Does it say when?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Abena has the ticket. She chased them Friday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Great. I'll leave it with her.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: The sensor by the stairs does the same thing. It thinks the cleaner is a ghost.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That one's mine to check. I'll look tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Can we get back? Chidi needs an answer this week or he loses the slot.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, yes. So where are we.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'll say one thing. If I'd known the spray existed, I wouldn't have pushed the concrete so hard in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm still not saying I love vinyl. I'm saying I can't argue with nine pounds.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, we've been going around this since October.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: I know. Um, I think, I think I have what I need. Sorry, Dmitri, did you want to-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: No, I'm fine. The timing works and the money works. I just want the letter.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: You'll get the letter. Amara said.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay. So, uh, luxury vinyl plank across the whole ground floor, with the sprayed membrane under the east half only. That's the floor.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Great. I'll ring Chidi after this.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Please. Tell him we're sorry about the, the back and forth.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: He's used to it by now. He said everyone changes their mind about floors.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Do we tell the acoustics people?

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Um, I think maybe just send Alejandra the data sheet, as a courtesy.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: I'll do that too.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: And I'll want to see the sample again. The grey one.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: It's in my bag. Still.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's always in your bag.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Because you never look at it.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Anything else? The, uh, sandwiches, we did those.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Numbers from Amara, yes.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I need to go, I've got the alarm company again.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Oh, yes, go. Thanks, Dmitri.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: Amara
utterances.text: Bye, I'll message you the letter.

utterances.speaker: Sana
utterances.text: Okay, bye, everyone.
